notFormalized.title: Theorem 11.3.9, the boundary operations of Definition 9.3.8 along equivalences
notFormalized.label: §11.3, Theorem 11.3.9, p. 542 (2017: Theorem 11.7, p. 395)
notFormalized.book: The boundary orientation $\hat T_{\partial\Theta}$ of Definition 9.3.10 is carried by generalized isomorphisms: $\partial(f_*\hat\Theta) = f_*(\partial\hat\Theta)$, independently of the representative.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized since the first edition of this page** (V11.25), for the intrinsic boundary orientation. sc-diffeomorphisms preserve $T^R_xX$, $C_xX$, the reduced codimension and the boundary operation of Definition 9.3.8 (`boundaryOp_map_tangentMapOn`), and so do equivalences and the fibre inverses (`EpFunctor.isReducedBoundaryTransfer_tangentMor`, `EpFunctor.isReducedBoundaryTransfer_fibreInv`); \"$d_M(x)$ is preserved\" is read for the reduced codimension of $T_xM$, which for tame $M$ is $d_M(x)$. So Theorem 11.3.9 holds for the generalized isomorphism itself, with $\hat T_{\partial\Theta}$ = `boundaryOrientation` (Definition 9.3.10, V9.38), with no transfer hypothesis (`EPLoc.theorem_11_3_9_push_boundaryOrientation`, `EPLoc.theorem_11_3_9_pull_boundaryOrientation`). For Chapter 9's `boundaryLift boundaryOp` it takes the tameness of $f_*\hat\Theta$ (`EPLoc.theorem_11_3_9_push_boundaryOp`), and `IsBoundaryTransfer` for `boundaryOp` takes `CarriesTameTangents`, since the restriction of sc-diffeomorphisms to tame sub-M-polyfolds is not formalized (Findings, Chapter 11, item 45).

notFormalized.title: §11.4, integration up to equivalence
notFormalized.label: §11.4, Theorems 11.4.1, 11.4.2, 11.4.4, 11.4.5 and Remark 11.4.3, pp. 542–546 (2017: Theorems 11.8, 11.9, Remark 11.3, pp. 396–399)
notFormalized.book: Generalized isomorphisms transform the canonical measures and the canonical boundary measures (and their effective versions) of oriented compact branched ep⁺-subgroupoids by $|f|$.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized in part** (2026-11-13; V11.27–V11.29; `Chapter11/GapP2_H4Compat.lean`, `GapP2_H4CrossChart.lean`, `GapP2_H4CompatInst.lean`, `GapP2_H4Move.lean`, `GapP2_H4Pairs.lean`, `GapP2_H4Measure.lean`, `GapP2_H4Diagram.lean`, `GapP2_H4Eff.lean`, `GapP2_H4EffDiagram.lean`, `GapP2_H4MSheets.lean`, `GapP2_H4BdGeom.lean`, `GapP2_H4Bd.lean`, `GapP2_H4BdDiagram.lean`). Theorem 11.4.1 and Remark 11.4.3 are formalized for the canonical measures of Theorem 9.5.4 built from the concrete sheet integrals of Chapter 9 (dimension $n\ge1$, forms $\Omega^n_{ep,\infty}$), with no added hypothesis. The proof follows the text: structures are moved along the local sc-diffeomorphisms of an equivalence, (11.12) = (11.13), uniqueness of the glued measure, then $G_*F^*$ for $X \leftarrow A \rightarrow Y$; $|f|$ is shown to map $\mathcal L(|\mathrm{supp}\,\Theta|)$ onto $\mathcal L(|\mathrm{supp}\,f_*\Theta|)$. Theorem 11.4.2 is formalized in the same way for the effective measures of Theorem 9.5.5 (`GapP2_H4Eff.lean`, `GapP2_H4EffDiagram.lean`): under LUC, $\sharp G_x^{eff} = \sharp G_y^{eff}$ along the local sc-diffeomorphisms of an equivalence. Theorems 11.4.4 and 11.4.5 are formalized for the boundary measures of Theorems 9.5.15/9.5.16 in their Lean form (`Chapter9/GapP2_E7_BoundaryMeasure.lean`): the boundary sheets of a moved structure are the moved boundary sheets with the moved boundary orientation, the multi-chart integrals change variables along the local sc-diffeomorphisms, and $|f|$ maps $\mathcal L(\partial S)$ onto $\mathcal L(\partial S)$. They carry the class hypothesis `hcov` of Theorems 9.5.15/9.5.16 (the nonempty boundary sheets lie in the integration class), which is not derived from the text near the corners of the sheets; it passes along generalized isomorphisms (`hcovB_pull`, `hcovB_push`, `Diagram.hcovB_pullTheta`, `Diagram.hcovB_pushTheta`), and it holds for compact boundary sheets (`hcov_msheets_of_isCompact`) and, with $\partial S \ne \emptyset$, for the closed upper hemisphere in $[0,\infty)\times\mathbb R^2$ (`E8W.e8w_hcov`, `EP.hcovB_of_hcovS`); the dimension is $n = m + 1$ with $m > 0$. **Not formalized**: the class condition near the corners of the sheets (the closed faces as submanifolds, estimate 800–1,200 lines; gap G.109) and the case $n = 1$ of Theorems 11.4.4/11.4.5 (Findings, Chapter 11, item 50).

notFormalized.title: Proposition 11.5.1, conditions (1) and (2) of Definition 8.3.5
notFormalized.label: §11.5, Proposition 11.5.1, p. 547 (2017: Proposition 11.6, p. 399)
notFormalized.book: $[D]^*N'$ and $[D]_*N$ of auxiliary norms are auxiliary norms.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized** (2026-11-09) in `Chapter11/AuxiliaryNormTransport2021.lean`. Condition (1) transfers the complete fibre norm along the linear isomorphism $\Psi_x \circ \Phi_x^{-1} \circ \mu(\sigma^{-1}, \cdot)$ of $W_{0,1}$-fibres. Condition (2) lifts $h_k$ through a local inverse of $t$ and of $\varphi$, applies (2) for $N'$, and returns through the level-1 local inverse of $\Phi$ and the continuity of $\mu[1]$. The push-forward is the pull-back along the reversed diagram. `GenSBMap.proposition_11_5_1_book` states Proposition 11.5.1 in full, with no added hypothesis (V11.30) (Findings, Chapter 11, items 60, 81).

notFormalized.label: §11.5, Lemma 11.5.2 and Proposition 11.5.3, pp. 547–549 (2017: Lemma 11.7, Proposition 11.7, pp. 400–401)
notFormalized.book: Push-forwards and pull-backs of sc⁺-multisections are sc⁺-multisections: their local section structures are carried along.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized** (2026-11-09) in `Chapter11/MultisectionLocalStructure2021.lean`. That file adds Definition 13.2.1 (`IsScPlusMultisection`, satisfiable by the multisection of the zero section). The local section structures go along a strong bundle equivalence both ways, by the text's construction with a local inverse of the target map. `lemma_11_5_2_book` and `GenSBMap.proposition_11_5_3_book` state Lemma 11.5.2 and Proposition 11.5.3 for sc⁺-multisections, with no added hypothesis (V11.31, V11.32). notFormalized.title: the localization $\mathcal{PC}(E^{-1})$ and $I : \mathcal{PC} \to \mathcal{PC}(E^{-1})$
notFormalized.label: §11.6, after Proposition 11.6.8, pp. 561–563 (2017 pp. 410–412)
notFormalized.book: Classes of diagrams under common refinement form the morphisms of a category $\mathcal{PC}(E^{-1})$, with composition through weak fibred products, and $I : \mathcal{PC} \to \mathcal{PC}(E^{-1})$ maps equivalences to isomorphisms; the well-definedness of the composition is left to the reader.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized** (2026-11-12) in `Chapter11/GapP2_HPCLocalization.lean` (V11.43). Classes of diagrams under common refinement are the morphisms of a category `PCLoc` ($\mathcal{PC}(E^{-1})$), composed through the weak fibred products of Theorem 11.6.6; the class of the composite does not depend on the representatives (`hasCommonRefinement_comp`, the step left to the reader), via maps of weak fibred products into `PC.fibred` built from natural transformations (`fibredLift`), which are equivalences by two out of three. $I : \mathcal{PC} \to \mathcal{PC}(E^{-1})$ maps equivalences to isomorphisms (`isIso_I_map`), every morphism is $I(\Gamma)^{-1} I(\varepsilon)$ (`homMk_eq`), and $[F \leftarrow A \rightarrow F']$ with both legs equivalences is invertible with the inverse of the text (`inv_homMk`). The middle of the composite is $A' \times_{F'} A$ (Theorem 11.6.6 is formalized with the equivalence on the left) (Findings, Chapter 11, item 76).

notFormalized.title: Remark 11.6.9, the category of proper strong bundle coverings
notFormalized.label: §11.6, Remark 11.6.9, pp. 563–566 (2017: Remark 11.4, pp. 412–413)
notFormalized.book: Proper strong bundle coverings, their functors and equivalences, the analogue of Theorem 11.6.6 and the localization, the details left to the reader.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized** (2026-11-12, `Chapter11/GapP2_H2SBPC.lean`, `GapP2_H3SBPullback.lean`, `GapP2_H3SBFibred.lean`, `GapP2_H3SBLocalization.lean`; V11.42). The category SBPC (objects: strong bundle functors $A$ over $F$ satisfying Definition 8.5.9; morphisms: commutative cubes), the class $E_{SBPC}$ (read: both components strong bundle equivalences; the text does not define it), and $SBPC[E^{-1}]$ with its universal property. Theorem 11.6.6 for SBPC: the weak fibred product of strong bundles over that of the bases is a proper strong bundle covering, $\pi_{(A'',F'')}$ is an equivalence and the square commutes up to natural equivalence (`SBPC.theorem_11_6_6`). $SBPC[E^{-1}]$ is described by diagrams under common refinement, as for $\mathcal{PC}(E^{-1})$ (`SBPCLoc`), with the comparison functor from the universal localization (Findings, Chapter 11, items 76–78).
